title: Physics world (Rapier)
description: Rigid-body physics and walking characters for any three.js object, on the Rapier engine (WebAssembly, Apache-2.0). createWorld() steps at a fixed 60 Hz; attach(object) gives it a dynamic, fixed, kinematic or platform body whose shape comes from the object itself: a box around it, a ball, an upright cylinder (round tables), a convex hull of a GLB's vertices, or exact triangles for level geometry. character() is a capsule that walks, slides along walls, climbs steps and slopes, shoves loose things and rides moving floors. Dynamic bodies can be grabbed and thrown. Collisions report impact speed for sounds, raycasts find what's in front of you. Units are metres: size models from their measured size. Rapier loads with the first world, so a game whose physics can't load still runs. The game maps @dimforge/rapier3d-compat@0.21.0 in its import map.
author: the internet slop warehouse

made.tool: Claude Code; Rapier 0.21.0 (Apache-2.0) is imported, not copied

exports.name: createWorld
exports.signature: createWorld({ gravity, step, maxSteps }) → Promise<{ update(dt), raycast(origin, direction, far), dispose(), raw, rapier }>
exports.does: starts Rapier and a world; update(dt) steps at a fixed rate then moves every attached object

exports.name: attach
exports.signature: attach(object, opts) → { update(), dispose(), body, collider, impulse([x,y,z]), velocity([x,y,z]?), grab(), release([x,y,z]?) }
exports.does: gives an object a rigid body and a collider shaped from its meshes

exports.name: character
exports.signature: character(world, { position, radius, height, step, slope, snap, push, mass }) → { walk(vx, vz), jump(speed), ride(dy), teleport([x,y,z]), ignore(collider), unignore(collider), position, grounded, dispose() }
exports.does: a walking capsule (feet at position) moved by Rapier's character controller inside the fixed steps

options.name: body
options.does: dynamic falls and collides; fixed never moves (floors, walls); kinematic follows the object as you move it and pushes dynamic bodies; platform is a floor you move that characters walk on and ride (an elevator)

options.name: shape
options.does: box or ball around the object, hull of its vertices (good for GLBs), mesh of its exact triangles (fixed bodies only)

options.name: mass
options.does: the body's mass; otherwise density × volume

options.name: density
options.does: mass = density × volume in m³; what matters is the ratio between bodies (a ball at 9 knocks over crates at 0.6)

options.name: damping
options.does: slows spinning; 0.5–2 lets a hull resting on uneven legs (a chair) settle and sleep instead of rocking

options.name: ccd
options.does: continuous collision for fast things (bullets, thrown balls) so they don't pass through thin walls

hooks.name: onContact
hooks.does: ({ other, speed }) when this body starts touching another: play a sound, deal damage, score

title: Tower topple
description: Knock a tower of crates off the table with eight balls: tap or click to throw. Every win adds a layer. A small physics-world demo, meant to be remixed: swap the crates for any GLB, change the table, add a slingshot. Crates and barrels collide with real physics; harder hits sound harder.
author: the internet slop warehouse

title: Add physics to a warehouse game
description: Agent skill (SKILL.md for Claude Code and Codex): give a three.js game real rigid-body physics with the physics-world part (Rapier): the import map line, worlds and bodies, choosing shapes for GLBs, metres and measured sizes, throwing, contacts for sound and damage, raycasts, and the mistakes that make physics jitter, explode or tunnel. Tower topple is the worked example.
author: the internet slop warehouse
